import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    customer_profile = inputs["customer_profile"].copy()
    profile_changes = inputs["profile_changes"].copy()
    
    # Ensure proper types
    customer_profile["customer_id"] = customer_profile["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    customer_profile["updated_seq"] = customer_profile["updated_seq"].astype("int64")
    profile_changes["change_seq"] = profile_changes["change_seq"].astype("int64")
    profile_changes["customer_id"] = profile_changes["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    
    # Convert email to lowercase and trimmed for profile
    customer_profile["email"] = customer_profile["email"].apply(
        lambda x: str(x).lower().strip() if pd.notna(x) else x
    )
    
    # Initialize result as copy of customer_profile
    result_rows = {}
    
    # First, populate with existing customers
    for _, row in customer_profile.iterrows():
        cid = row["customer_id"]
        result_rows[cid] = {
            "customer_id": cid,
            "email": row["email"],
            "phone": row["phone"],
            "tier": row["tier"],
            "updated_seq": row["updated_seq"],
        }
    
    # Process changes grouped by customer_id, sorted by change_seq
    changes_by_customer = profile_changes.groupby("customer_id")
    
    for customer_id, group in changes_by_customer:
        # Sort by change_seq to process in order
        group = group.sort_values("change_seq").reset_index(drop=True)
        
        # Get current state or initialize if new customer
        if customer_id in result_rows:
            current = result_rows[customer_id]
            current_seq = current["updated_seq"]
            is_new_customer = False
        else:
            current = {
                "customer_id": customer_id,
                "email": None,
                "phone": None,
                "tier": None,
                "updated_seq": None,
            }
            current_seq = -1
            is_new_customer = True
        
        # Process each change
        for _, change in group.iterrows():
            change_seq = change["change_seq"]
            
            # Skip if change_seq <= updated_seq (already applied)
            if current_seq >= change_seq:
                continue
            
            # Save previous state to detect no-ops
            prev_email = current["email"]
            prev_phone = current["phone"]
            prev_tier = current["tier"]
            
            # Apply field rules
            # email: NULL means no change; '<<NULL>>' means set to NULL; else set to value
            if pd.notna(change["email"]):
                if change["email"] == "<<NULL>>":
                    current["email"] = None
                else:
                    current["email"] = str(change["email"]).lower().strip()
            
            # phone: NULL means no change; '<<NULL>>' means set to NULL; else set to value
            if pd.notna(change["phone"]):
                if change["phone"] == "<<NULL>>":
                    current["phone"] = None
                else:
                    current["phone"] = change["phone"]
            
            # tier: NULL means no change; '<<NULL>>' means set to NULL; else set to value
            if pd.notna(change["tier"]):
                if change["tier"] == "<<NULL>>":
                    current["tier"] = None
                else:
                    current["tier"] = change["tier"]
            
            # Check if this is a no-op (all fields unchanged, NULL-safe comparison)
            is_noop = (
                (prev_email == current["email"] or (pd.isna(prev_email) and pd.isna(current["email"])))
                and (prev_phone == current["phone"] or (pd.isna(prev_phone) and pd.isna(current["phone"])))
                and (prev_tier == current["tier"] or (pd.isna(prev_tier) and pd.isna(current["tier"])))
            )
            
            # For new customers, creation is never a no-op
            if is_new_customer or not is_noop:
                current["updated_seq"] = change_seq
                is_new_customer = False
            # Note: if is_noop and not new customer, updated_seq is NOT advanced
        
        result_rows[customer_id] = current
    
    # Convert result to DataFrame
    result_data = list(result_rows.values())
    new_profile = pd.DataFrame(result_data)
    
    # Ensure columns are in the right order and types
    new_profile = new_profile[["customer_id", "email", "phone", "tier", "updated_seq"]]
    new_profile["customer_id"] = new_profile["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    new_profile["updated_seq"] = new_profile["updated_seq"].astype("int64")
    
    return {"new_profile": new_profile}
